incidents.victim: Government, education, media, technology and gaming web servers (Brazil, Bolivia, Canada, Vietnam, China)
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — China-based (SEO fraud and data theft)
incidents.vector: A Chinese-speaking group exploited known one-day flaws in internet-facing servers (Zimbra, Nacos, AjaxPro) and used agentic AI to automate exploitation, then deployed the new cross-platform SPECTRE backdoor with a Linux rootkit and BYOVD tooling to disable EDR.
incidents.impact: Cisco Talos found the actor (UAT-10147) running SEO fraud and data theft at scale against roughly 170,000 target URLs, using AI-assisted playbooks, exploit automation and custom malware to blind endpoint defenses.

incidents.victim: Academics, aerospace/defense staff, government officials and think tanks (Europe and US)
incidents.vector: Three suspected Russian clusters (UNC6293, UNC7005, UNC5976, tied to the group formerly called APT29) abused legitimate authentication flows — app-password phishing, OAuth and device-code phishing, and WhatsApp device linking — to hijack personal accounts without triggering MFA.
incidents.impact: Google Threat Intelligence Group reported persistent, adaptive social-engineering campaigns that compromise the personal accounts of individuals of interest to the Russian state to collect intelligence.

incidents.victim: US critical infrastructure operators using Siemens S7 PLCs (water, energy, chemical, manufacturing, food, commercial facilities)
incidents.vector: Threat actors used internet scanning services to find exposed or poorly segmented Siemens S7 PLCs and deployed AI-generated Python exploitation scripts (built on snap7) disguised as legitimate monitoring tools to gain read/write access via the S7comm protocol.
incidents.impact: NSA, CISA, FBI, DOE and EPA warned this is an active — not theoretical — threat, assessed as persistent reconnaissance and pre-positioning that could later disrupt industrial processes, cause safety incidents or damage equipment.

incidents.victim: Latvia Road Traffic Safety Directorate (CSDD)
incidents.vector: Attackers exploited a vulnerability in an internet-exposed CSDD system where several mandatory cybersecurity requirements had not been met, accessing historical vehicle-payment receipt data dating back to 2008.
incidents.impact: Data on more than 1.2 million people (about two-thirds of Latvia's population) and 200,000 businesses was exposed; the breach triggered the resignation of the agency's supervisory board and a political crisis, with a second attack blocked days later.

incidents.victim: CareCloud (electronic health record provider)
incidents.vector: A hacker gained access to one of CareCloud's AWS environments for roughly six days in March and exfiltrated data before being detected.
incidents.impact: CareCloud told regulators that 3.76 million people had personal, Social Security, payment card, medical and insurance data exposed; the company serves more than 45,000 providers. No group claimed the attack.

incidents.victim: PTC Windchill/FlexPLM customers (manufacturing, aerospace, automotive; GE, Philips, Shell, Toast, Zebra named)
incidents.vector: The Clop group mass-exploited a critical unauthenticated RCE zero-day (CVE-2026-12569) in PTC's Windchill and FlexPLM products, using a custom Windchill-specific web shell for credential theft, malware delivery and large-scale data exfiltration.
incidents.impact: Clop claims data theft from dozens of organizations, including some of the world's largest public companies; exploitation began in early June before the June 17 disclosure and the fallout is still emerging.

incidents.victim: Taiwan government agencies (Ministry of Digital Affairs)
incidents.vector: A Chinese-language operator used a multi-agent AI framework (built on OpenClaw/Hermes) running up to eight subagents to autonomously conduct reconnaissance, crack credentials, find and exploit vulnerabilities, exfiltrate personnel records and install backdoors across 12 attack waves.
incidents.impact: Described by researchers as the first 'near-autonomous' AI attack on a nation-state; Taiwan's MODA confirmed abnormal AI-driven attacks on government agencies in July that used backup and test environments as springboards.

incidents.victim: Corporate travelers and hospitality/conference Wi-Fi networks worldwide
incidents.vector: A Midnight Blizzard subgroup (Storm-2945) manipulated DNS and HTTP traffic on captive-portal hotel and conference networks to redirect users through attacker infrastructure, delivering fake browser/OS 'updates' via ClickFix that installed the Go-based CornFlake RAT.
incidents.impact: Microsoft's CaptiveCrunch findings describe widespread compromise of hospitality Wi-Fi across multiple countries, with the RAT stealing credentials and session tokens, keylogging and enabling audio/video surveillance to collect intelligence on travelers.

incidents.victim: 500+ organizations worldwide, especially healthcare and public health
incidents.vector: The Medusa ransomware-as-a-service operation buys initial access from brokers and exploits unpatched software (e.g., Fortra GoAnywhere CVE-2025-10035, BeyondTrust CVE-2026-1731), often weaponizing new exploits within 24 hours and using double extortion.
incidents.impact: An updated FBI/CISA/HHS advisory reports Medusa has now hit more than 500 victims (up from 300), with a strong healthcare focus; the group previously shut down the University of Mississippi Medical Center.

incidents.victim: 144 US and 178 foreign universities, 42 US companies, government agencies (incl. HBO)
incidents.vector: Members of the Iran-based Mabna Institute ran spearphishing campaigns against more than 100,000 professor accounts, using stolen credentials to access research systems and email inboxes on behalf of the IRGC and other Iranian entities.
incidents.impact: DOJ unsealed a superseding indictment charging 17 Iranians in a campaign that stole 31.5 terabytes of academic data and IP; a $10 million reward was offered for five defendants. The underlying intrusions ran 2013-2017.

incidents.victim: Fortune 500 enterprises (McDonald's, Vodafone, Kyndryl, Gap, InterContinental, Wyndham reportedly)
incidents.vector: An actor using the handle 'TheHatman' claims to have used compromised credentials, MFA fatigue and password spraying to access victims' Microsoft Entra (Azure) tenants and exfiltrate employee data.
incidents.impact: From Aug 1-17 the actor advertised sensitive employee records from about a dozen large enterprises for sale across cybercrime forums; Unit 42 has not verified a specific intrusion vector but is tracking the activity.

incidents.victim: 1,100+ companies (software, staffing, healthcare, fintech) hiring remote workers
incidents.vector: North Korean IT workers (tracked as PurpleDelta, likely operating from China) used 22+ fabricated personas, AI-generated photos, custom ChatGPT assistants and real-time AI interview tools to fraudulently obtain remote technical jobs.
incidents.impact: Recorded Future assesses operators were actively employed at ten or more organizations, posing an ongoing insider threat, recording internal meetings and funneling earnings to the North Korean regime's weapons programs.

incidents.victim: Internet-exposed Fortinet, Sophos and MSSQL devices
incidents.vector: In the 'FortiBleed' campaign, attackers ran large-scale password spraying with a curated list built from prior breaches, extracted device configuration files (including stored credentials), cracked them offline and reused them to gain persistent admin access.
incidents.impact: Unit 42 reports an initial access broker on a Russian-language forum claimed responsibility and is selling harvested credentials; the multi-stage campaign continues to expand its password list against new targets.

incidents.victim: Winnipeg Health Sciences Centre
incidents.vector: A ransomware attack disabled building systems at Manitoba's largest hospital, including access-control doors and heating, ventilation and air conditioning.
incidents.impact: The hospital increased on-site security while the access-card system was down; it said patient care and clinical operations were not impacted.

incidents.victim: Berlin city government (urban development and mobility/transport ministries)
incidents.vector: Attackers allegedly exploited a vulnerability in the IT systems of one of the affected ministries; two ministries were isolated from the state network as a precaution.
incidents.impact: Both ministries were cut off from email and internet, forcing staff to use phone, text and fax; some public services such as housing-benefit processing were disrupted. Attribution and data impact remain unclear.

incidents.victim: University of Texas at San Antonio
incidents.vector: The university detected threat activity at the edge of its academic network over the weekend and took systems, including phones, offline in response.
incidents.impact: The 40,000-student university faced disruptions to course sign-up and payment systems as classes began, extended payment deadlines and planned a full password reset; it says no evidence of data exfiltration was found.

incidents.victim: Ransomware victims of DragonForce, Settra and Anubis affiliates
incidents.vector: An actor calling itself 'Ransom Busters' emails cyberattack victims — sometimes before the breach is public — falsely posing as an incident-recovery service and offering to delete stolen data and supply decryption keys for a fee.
incidents.impact: GuidePoint assesses this is a single ransomware affiliate working across multiple RaaS operations, using its affiliate access to divert ransom payments away from the original gangs by charging victims $20,000-$60,000.

incidents.victim: Enterprise Microsoft 365 / Azure environments
incidents.vector: The 'TwinLoot' Python malware framework runs its entire command-and-control from inside Microsoft cloud services — SharePoint and Graph API for C2, Teams TURN relays for interactive access and the victim's Edge browser to disguise traffic — while harvesting credentials via fake lock screens.
incidents.impact: Ontinue discovered the framework during a July incident; it provides a reverse SOCKS5 pivot for lateral movement and uses a novel offline-forged profile-hive persistence technique, with all activity blending into legitimate cloud traffic.

incidents.victim: Slovak national traffic-monitoring system (279 speed cameras)
incidents.vector: Slovakia's NBU found that NERO R-ONE speed cameras — rebranded Russian CORDON PRO.M devices bought via a no-bid contract from a Cyprus shell company — contained a backdoor that executes code sent by SMS from hardcoded Russian phone numbers.
incidents.impact: The agency also found SecureBoot disabled, a vulnerable web portal and unauthenticated live-stream access; 279 cameras from a €30 million EU-funded project were installed before deployment was paused for an independent audit.

incidents.victim: Bluesky and GitHub
incidents.vector: An Iranian hacktivist group known as the '313 Team' launched distributed denial-of-service attacks against the two platforms on consecutive days.
incidents.impact: The DDoS attacks caused prolonged outages at both companies; Bluesky said it upgraded its defenses in response. The same group ran a prior DDoS wave in April.

incidents.victim: Wildberries (Russian e-commerce marketplace)
incidents.vector: Ukraine's GUR, working with the pro-Ukraine Cyber Corps group, claimed a cyberattack against Wildberries' customer service, contact centers and payment infrastructure, timed with drone strikes on a company warehouse.
incidents.impact: The disruption to call centers and payment systems was additive to an ongoing kinetic campaign; analysts assessed the cyber impact as annoying rather than materially amplifying the drone strikes, but valuable as propaganda.

incidents.victim: 165+ Snowflake customers (incl. AT&T, Ticketmaster, LendingTree, Advance Auto Parts, Neiman Marcus)
incidents.vector: Between February and October 2024, Connor Riley Moucka ('Judische'/'Waifu') and co-conspirators used stolen credentials to access Snowflake customer accounts that did not enforce MFA, then extorted the victims.
incidents.impact: Moucka pleaded guilty to computer fraud, wire fraud, aggravated identity theft and conspiracy, admitting to stealing 100M+ AT&T call/text records and over $2.5M in ransom payments; sentencing is set for Oct 27.
